meal.title: Read input with scanf
meal.objective: Use scanf with a format specifier and ampersand to read integers

voice.script: How does a program hear what you type? That's what scanf does. Think of printf as shouting out text, while scanf is listening in. First, you need a way to tell the computer what kind of data to expect. A format specifier is a short code, like %d, that says "I want an integer". Next, you must give scanf the address of the variable where the number will live. The ampersand symbol provides that address, like a mailbox number for the value. So when you write scanf, you write the format specifier inside quotes, then a comma, then the ampersand and the variable name. When the user types a number and hits enter, scanf stores that number at the given address, ready for the program to use.
